trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (mean over pool3) and the verdict is 'indistinguishable' — the runner-up is not statistically better. The series is trend-dominated with moderate ranking stability and correlated error groups, so a broad stable-pool mean is the right kind of combination. With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights are high-variance, and the full pool is contaminated by a model with RMSE 2197. The pool3 mean already captures the trend robustly while excluding the worst performers. I should accept.

action_args.justification: The series is strongly trend-dominated (trend strength 0.96, no seasonality) with moderate ranking stability (Kendall tau 0.446) and correlated error groups among the top models. A mean over the 9 most consistently-ranked models (pool3) captures the shared trend signal while averaging out idiosyncratic errors, and excludes the worst performers (RMSE up to 2197) that contaminate the full-pool mean/median. With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights are high-variance and the leader's margin over the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, so the robust stable-pool mean is the safest choice.
